entries.title: Sid Gillman and passing-offense development
entries.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame identifies Sid Gillman as a leading authority on forward-passing offense and describes his Chargers as a major influence on professional passing strategy.
principles: Treat Gillman as an important node in the historical passing-offense graph.
Study his concepts separately before asserting direct lineage to a later system.
limitations: Influence does not imply that every later vertical passing concept originated with Gillman.
fantasyImplications: Historical context only until linked to modern observed concepts and validated fantasy effects.

entries.title: Don Coryell offensive record and influence
entries.summary: Coryell revived the St. Louis Cardinals and San Diego Chargers; the Hall of Fame records that his Chargers led the NFL in passing seven of eight seasons and consistently ranked among the league's top offenses.
principles: Study Coryell as both a historical coach and an offensive-system innovator.
Separate documented outcomes from later schematic interpretations.
limitations: Team passing rank alone does not identify which concepts caused success.
fantasyImplications: Historical foundation for later study of role creation, field stretching and mismatch usage; no direct ranking adjustment.

entries.title: Coryell offense stressed the whole field and multiple eligible receivers
entries.summary: A Hall of Fame historical feature quotes former Chargers receiver John Jefferson describing Coryell's offense as using the entire field and all eligible skill-position weapons, with plays designed to involve multiple receivers and find the open man.
principles: Model system intent as distributing stress across the field and eligible receivers.
Preserve this as participant testimony rather than universal schematic law.
limitations: Participant recollection is strong historical evidence but not a complete playbook taxonomy.
fantasyImplications: Generates hypotheses about how system structure can create opportunity across WR/TE/RB roles; must be tested in modern descendants.

entries.title: Coryell option-passing response to coverage
entries.summary: The Hall of Fame's Air Coryell history describes a St. Louis option-passing system in which the quarterback evaluated pass coverage and attacked its weak area.
principles: Connect offensive decisions to defensive structure.
Treat coverage recognition as part of offensive problem solving, not merely a post-play statistic.
limitations: The source does not provide a complete rule set for the option-passing system.
fantasyImplications: Supports investigation of offense-versus-coverage interaction as a fantasy-relevant hypothesis.

entries.title: Coryell and tight-end mismatch deployment
entries.summary: Kellen Winslow credited Coryell with changing how the tight end could be deployed; Hall of Fame material describes two-tight-end personnel being used to preserve blocking while creating receiving mismatches.
principles: Personnel can be used to force defensive matchup decisions.
Position labels do not fully describe receiving deployment.
limitations: Do not infer that all Coryell descendants use two-tight-end personnel similarly.
fantasyImplications: Historical basis for studying how personnel/mismatch design changes TE route and target opportunity.

entries.title: NFL shift terminology baseline
entries.summary: NFL Football Operations defines a shift as simultaneous pre-snap movement of two or more offensive players. Super SAGE should preserve official terminology and distinguish shifts from other pre-snap movement.
principles: Use official rule terminology as baseline.
Do not casually collapse shift and motion into one label when analyzing play structure.
limitations: This entry establishes terminology, not every legal-motion rule.
fantasyImplications: Improves data classification; no direct fantasy adjustment.
